Hi Matt —

Thanks — helpful set of questions. I put together a short decision tree and a per-control mapping for the SIG items you mentioned. High-level summary here, full artifacts attached: hosting-decision-tree.pdf and sig-answers-risehold.xlsx.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood manages the control plane and key custody by default. We hold KMS-managed keys for customer workloads in our managed offering; customers may request a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) option in higher tiers. Evidence: soc2-summary.pdf excerpt + KMS integration diagram (architecture-diagram.pdf).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Tenant-isolated GPU pools with network ACLs. Key custody is configurable — default is Redwood-managed keys; for enterprise Dedicated contracts we support customer-managed KMS (customer keys stored in their cloud or Redwood-managed HSM with restricted access). Evidence: sig-answers-risehold.xlsx rows 12-20 + architecture-diagram.pdf.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer control plane and networking. Key custody is customer-controlled; Redwood provides optional on-prem components but does not retain customer keys. Evidence: hosting-decision-tree.pdf + runbook links in the Drive folder (linked below).

Retention and Access to Logs:  
- Hosted: Default 90 days of request/trace logs; retention extensions available as an add-on up to 7 years. Access: Redwood SRE + designated customer admins (RBAC and audit trail).
- Dedicated: Default 180 days; can be configured per contract. Access: customer admins + optional Redwood on-call (explicit ACLs).
- Private: Control plane hosted by customer — retention and access are set by customer policies.

Network Isolation:
- Hosted: Multi-tenant with workload isolation (namespace-level) + egress controls.
- Dedicated: Single-tenant GPU pools; cross-tenant networking blocked; customers get VPC peering options and private endpoints.
- Private: Full customer-managed network.

Attachments in this message: hosting-decision-tree.pdf, sig-answers-risehold.xlsx, architecture-diagram.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf.

Matt — quick technical clarifications to add to Hannah's mapping: 

1) Runtime KV cache and model context: For Hosted we keep ephemeral KV caches that are scoped to the request and purged after response completion; no long-term model-state storage. For Dedicated, the runtime offers the same purging behavior by default; customers can opt into longer-lived caches for performance but that requires explicit configuration and is called out in the sig-answers spreadsheet. For Private, the cache lifecycle is controlled by the customer's deployment config.

2) Fallbacks & model routing: In Hosted we may route to a compatible model variant for availability (standard policy) — we maintain an internal compatibility matrix; customer data is never routed to a different tenant. For Dedicated we route within the reserved pool. Private deployments follow whatever routing the customer's control plane implements.

3) Evidence pointers: Architecture diagram (attached) highlights where KMS calls happen and where logs are emitted. The drive link in Hannah's follow-up contains a sample KMS audit export and a sanitized runbook for log retrieval.

Happy to join the call to walk the runtime flow.

- Aditya
